key_insight: At-home accelerometry combined with machine learning captured motor impairment in children with ataxia-telangiectasia (A-T), with ankle scores also detecting disease progression.
clinical_relevance: Ankle-based scores may offer a sensitive outcome measure for A-T clinical trials; this study did not evaluate cancer drug discovery.
method: 43 children with classic A-T and 50 matched controls wore ankle and wrist accelerometers at home for one week.
Monitoring was repeated at 6- to 12-month intervals.
Machine-learning models combined 85 features per sensor site to estimate clinician-rated motor severity.
evidence_signal: Ankle scores correlated with BARS gait ratings (r = 0.88), showed high within-week reliability (ICC = 0.95), and detected progression in a matched subset (p = 0.0036), where BARS changes were not statistically significant.
watch_item: The relatively small pediatric cohort warrants independent validation before these scores are adopted as clinical-trial outcomes.
paper_title: At-home ankle and wrist accelerometry and machine learning capture motor impairment and disease progression in ataxia-telangiectasia
